title: Sumset A + A
content: **sumset A**: The sumset $A + A = \{a + b : a, b \in A\}$, computed as `(A ×ˢ A).image (fun p => p.1 + p.2)`. The Cartesian product `Finset.product` generates all pairs, and `Finset.image` applies the addition function, automatically removing duplicates. For an arithmetic progression of length $n$, $|A + A| = 2n - 1$ (small); for a random set, $|A + A| \approx |A|^2$ (large).

title: Product Set A · A
content: **productset A**: The product set $A \cdot A = \{a \cdot b : a, b \in A\}$, computed as `(A ×ˢ A).image (fun p => p.1 * p.2)`. For a geometric progression of ratio $r$, $|A \cdot A| = 2n - 1$ (small); for a random set, $|A \cdot A| \approx |A|^2$ (large). The key insight is that sets with small sumset (additive structure) tend to have large product set, and vice versa.

title: Sum-Product Maximum
content: **sumProductMax A**: The quantity $\max(|A+A|, |A \cdot A|)$, computed via `max (sumset A).card (productset A).card`. This is the central object of the conjecture—it captures the idea that at least one of the two operations must expand the set significantly. Marked `noncomputable` because it involves cardinality of image sets.

title: Erdős Problem #52: Sum-Product Conjecture
content: **ErdosProblem52**: The main conjecture as a `Prop` (not an axiom): $\forall \varepsilon > 0, \exists C > 0, \forall A$ with $|A| \geq 2$, $\text{sumProductMax}(A) \geq C \cdot |A|^{2-\varepsilon}$. Being a `def` rather than an `axiom` means this is the statement to be proved, not assumed. The exponent $2 - \varepsilon$ is the conjectured optimum, matching the trivial upper bound $|A|^2$. Carries a \$250 Erdős prize.

title: Erdős–Szemerédi Theorem (1983)
content: **erdos_szemeredi_theorem**: Axiomatizes the foundational result: $\exists c > 0, \forall A$ with $|A| \geq 2$, $\text{sumProductMax}(A) \geq |A|^{1+c}$. This was the first proof that the sum-product phenomenon is real—at least one of $|A+A|$ or $|A \cdot A|$ must grow super-linearly. The original constant $c$ was very small; subsequent work has steadily improved it.

title: Bloom's 2025 Bound
content: **bloom_bound**: Axiomatizes the current best bound: for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $N_0$ such that for $|A| \geq N_0$, $\text{sumProductMax}(A) \geq |A|^{1270/951 - \varepsilon}$. The rational exponent $1270/951 \approx 1.335$ improves on a long line of results (Elekes, Solymosi, Konyagin–Shkredov, Rudnev–Stevens). The gap to the conjectured $2 - \varepsilon$ remains substantial.

title: Trivial Lower Bounds
content: **sumset_card_ge** and **productset_card_ge**: Axiomatize the trivial lower bounds $|A| \leq |A+A|$ (for nonempty $A$) and $|A| \leq |A \cdot A|$ (when $0 \notin A$ and $|A| \geq 2$). The sumset bound holds because $a + 0 \in A + A$ for each $a$ if $0 \in A$, or more generally because the map $a \mapsto a + b_0$ is injective. The product set requires $0 \notin A$ to avoid collapsing products to 0.

title: Trivial Upper Bounds
content: **sumset_card_le** and **productset_card_le**: Axiomatize $|A+A| \leq |A|^2$ and $|A \cdot A| \leq |A|^2$. Both follow because the sumset (resp. product set) is the image of $A \times A$, which has $|A|^2$ elements. This shows the conjectured exponent $2 - \varepsilon$ is tight—it cannot be improved to $2 + \delta$.

title: m-Fold Sumset
content: **mfoldSumset A m**: The $m$-fold sumset $mA = \{a_1 + \cdots + a_m : a_i \in A\}$, defined recursively: $0A = \{0\}$ and $(n+1)A = (nA \times^s A).\text{image}(+)$. For an arithmetic progression, $|mA| = \Theta(m|A|)$; for a random set, $|mA| \approx |A|^m$.

title: m-Fold Product Set
content: **mfoldProductset A m**: The $m$-fold product set $A^m = \{a_1 \cdot \cdots \cdot a_m : a_i \in A\}$, defined recursively: $A^0 = \{1\}$ and $A^{n+1} = (A^n \times^s A).\text{image}(\cdot)$. For a geometric progression, $|A^m| = \Theta(m|A|)$; for a random set, $|A^m| \approx |A|^m$.

title: Generalized Sum-Product Conjecture
content: **GeneralizedSumProduct m**: The $m$-fold generalization: for $m \geq 2$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$, $\max(|mA|, |A^m|) \geq C \cdot |A|^{m-\varepsilon}$. This extends the pairwise conjecture ($m = 2$) to arbitrary fold. Defined as a `Prop` parameterized by $m$. The trivial upper bound $|A|^m$ shows the exponent $m - \varepsilon$ is optimal.

title: Connection to Problem 53
content: **sum_product_implies_many_representations**: Axiomatizes a weak consequence: $(|A+A| + |A \cdot A|) \geq |A|$ for $|A| \geq 2$. This trivial bound connects to Problem #53 (resolved by Chang 2003), which asks about sums and products of *distinct* subsets rather than pairwise operations. The sum-product conjecture implies strong forms of Problem #53.
